findings.description: The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data and its rendered contents can be retrieved by principals with EC2 instance/user-data access, exposing database credentials.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network address. This unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-reachable attack paths if security-group or routing controls change or are bypassed.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and snapshots unencrypted at rest.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. A compromised database host could use this unrestricted path for command-and-control or data exfiltration.
The EC2 application role grants all S3, EC2, and RDS actions against every resource. Compromise of the instance or its role credentials would enable broad account-wide access and modification.
